mentl/2f6ddea:
The ??-fan minted three integer seeds for every Int-shaped hole and then let
the proof gate reject the ones the type never admitted. The refinement was
one field away the whole time: enumerate_typed's TRefined arm recursed on the
BASE and dropped the predicate. It reads the predicate now, as a Domain.

Domain (types.mn) is an over-approximation by contract, and the contract is
what makes it safe to build from: a superset may decide what to CONSTRUCT
because it cuts no inhabitant, while the proof gate keeps deciding what to
ADMIT. Meet takes the decided side when one side is unreadable; join widens
to the top rather than claim a bound it cannot cover; a float refinement
reads DUndecided because strict-to-inclusive needs a predecessor and a float
has none (Hβ.verify.domain-over-reals names the open/closed form).

It is one walk, not a new one. ty_lo asked this same structure for the lower
bound alone and had no upper counterpart, so a consumer wanting a ceiling
would have grown a mirror family beside it. pred_lo and lo_best are gone:
ty_lo is now domain_lo(ty_domain(ty)), and the bound-meet is the domain-meet.
The read proves strictly more than before (self == n now yields a bound),
which is why it marched and ran the proof gate alone before anything was
built on it: CLEAN m2 == m3, census 0, proof-exactness 9 pass / 0 red.

The seed rule is boundary-value analysis and carries NO width constant — a
threshold would be a number nobody can derive. The bounds, plus the interior
value nearest zero, deduped:

  Int where 0 < self       -> [1, inf)  -> one seed, 1
  Int where 0 <= self <= 1 -> [0, 1]    -> two seeds, exactly the inhabitants
  Int where self == 7      -> {7}       -> one seed, the only value admitted
  unreadable predicate     -> the floor 0/1/-1, and the gate still judges

propose-demo/hole.mn answers Propose: 1, propose-fan-demo/bit.mn answers two
survivors 0 and 1, a bare Int hole answers th

it a measurement rather than a design choice: which prelude names does
the compiler mint that source never writes? Reachability seeded from
written names alone would miss them, so demand-linking is unsafe until
they are known.

Read off the artifact — quoted literals in the lowering, the wasm
backend, the parser, infer and pipeline, intersected against what lib
publishes — the answer is 44. The lowering and backend hold 28; parser
and infer add 16 more, including delay, not, concat, last, drop_last,
byte_at, byte_len, str_of_buf, str_payload and the float-render family.
It is a lower bound, not a proof: a name assembled by splicing a
fold_sig never appears as a literal. That limit is recorded rather than
papered over, and over-approximating the seed set is the safe direction.

The enumeration caught str_literal_5, which is the identity function.
Its comment claimed it allocates a small constant string from bytes with
the caller encoding the string as individual byte arguments — false
twice over, callers pass whole literals — and its text named the
bootstrap deleted on 2026-07-10. It survived by being load-bearing in
the wrong sense: a name-keyed entry in is_seq_op's cname chain and a
hand-written signature in infer's substrate table, so the type checker
special-cased an identity. Deleted whole: four call sites inlined, the
function gone, both table entries gone. One fewer name in the table that

touches — and measured exit=15 before the deletion and 15 after. Each
sentinel is a bit, so the code names which branch broke; the red test

The wheel emitted (memory 32768 65536 shared) — 2GB initial — while the
seed gives m2 the full 65536 pages. The bump allocator never grows
memory, so a wheel-scale compile through m3 'allocated' past 2GB
arithmetically and the first READ of such a record trapped OOB — m4

shared requires a max, and initial == max means the line never moves
under any thread). m2-tier: 8/8 rungs, 50/50 micros-through-m2.
mentl/2f4258f:
Dissolve PerformExpr into CallExpr — the bare op-call IS the canonical and
only form. SYNTAX.md: `perform` is format-lifted (E_RedundantPerform,
MachineApplicable); the env binding proves op-ness (EffectOpScheme) and the
op's TFun row carries Closed[eff] definitionally, so the CallExpr path infers
and lowers an op exactly as a bare call.

Carried-Truth: a bare CallExpr to an effect op ALREADY propagates the op's
effect row — infer_call unifies the op's TFun(.., Closed[eff]) against a fresh
open-row TFun; unify_row binds the row var to the residual; inf_add_row joins
it (proven by mn-ev2's bare d_log/g_mint inferring `with G + D`). So
infer_perform was a re-derivation of infer_call+unify_row, and PerformExpr a
parallel AST node for what CallExpr already is.

mentl/2f29e0f:
Five fixes that unblock the path to deleting Rust:

1. COW (Copy-on-Write) in Rust VM — handler state alias clearing enables
   in-place mutation for push/concat. 50K list builds in 0.08s (was freezing).
   Only clears handler state parameter locals (sound: always overwritten by Resume).

2. Index-based iterate in prelude — replaced O(N²) slice recursion with O(N)
   index loop. 140x speedup, 570x memory reduction for collection operations.

3. Dynamic handler dispatch via ~> — PushHandler sentinel 0xFFFF triggers
   runtime record-to-handler extraction. Records returned from functions
   work as handlers: make_logger("PROD") ~> worker().

4. WASM handler rewrite fix — extract_full_rewrite now produces the complete
   5-element entry format [name, params, pre_stmts, resume_value, updates].
   wasm_counter passes on wasmtime (count = 3). Root cause: nested variant
   matching bug in Rust VM (S(RecordExpr(_),_,_) matches any S) — workaround:
   two-step unwrap pattern in all compiler .lux files.

5. Prelude type cache — check_program_with(stmts, env, n) accepts pre-built
   environment. Pipeline caches prelude's 190 type bindings at import time.
   13.5s → 7.3s (46% faster). WASM compilation 135s → 84s.

mentl/2f5f88a:
Replace the flat EffectSet with row-polymorphic EffectRow, enabling
effect polymorphism. Functions without a `with` clause now get an open
effect row (fresh variable), making them generic over their caller's
effects. Functions with declared effects get closed rows. Handle
expressions remove effects from both open and closed rows via
`.without()`. Effect row unification binds row variables when open
rows meet closed rows.

Generators use the existing algebraic effect system: `yield` is a
builtin effect, `generate(func)` spawns func on an OS thread with a
rendezvous channel (capacity 0) providing natural backpressure.
`next(gen)` returns `Some(val)` or `None`. For-loops accept generators
natively alongside lists.

New builtins: generate, next, range. New example: generators.lux.
